questions.question: When a dataset contains many tuples with missing class labels, which handling technique is generally considered least effective according to the text?

options.D: Applying a machine‑learning model that can handle missing attributes

questions.explanation:
Ignoring the tuple is described as “not very effective” especially when missing values vary considerably across attributes [Page 6].

---

questions.question: Suppose a data collection instrument frequently records the default date “January 1” for unknown birthdays. Which term from the context best describes this phenomenon?
questions.explanation:
The text explicitly calls such default entries “disguised missing data” [Page 2].

---

questions.question: In a scenario where an attribute has a high percentage of missing values, which approach is most likely to be impractical according to the provided material?

options.A: Deleting all records with missing values for that attribute
options.D: Applying a global constant to replace missing entries

questions.explanation:
Manually filling missing values is noted as “time consuming and may not be feasible” for large datasets with many missing values [Page 6].

---

questions.question: Which of the following statements best captures the impact of noisy data on the data cleaning process as described in the context?

options.A: Noisy data are always removed before any analysis.
options.B: Noisy data can be smoothed, but outliers must still be identified.
options.C: Noisy data are irrelevant to data quality dimensions.
options.D: Noisy data are automatically corrected by database systems.

questions.explanation:
The text mentions that data cleaning “attempts to fill in missing values, smooth out noise while identifying outliers” [Page 6].

---

questions.question: If a dataset includes several attributes with missing values that differ greatly in the percentage of missingness, which handling method is likely to introduce the most bias?

options.A: Ignoring tuples with any missing attribute
options.B: Replacing missing values with the mean of each attribute
options.C: Using a k‑nearest‑neighbour imputation per attribute
options.D: Leaving the missing values as null and using algorithms that tolerate nulls

questions.explanation:
Ignoring tuples is especially poor when the percentage of missing values per attribute varies considerably, leading to biased samples [Page 6].

---

questions.question: According to the context, which data quality element is directly threatened by “incorrect data resulting from inconsistencies in naming conventions or data codes”?
questions.explanation:
Inconsistent naming or coding affects the “consistency” element of data quality [Page 2].

---

questions.question: When data are “contaminated, with some values out of range or of a different data type than expected,” which phase of the data preprocessing pipeline is most appropriate to address this issue?
questions.explanation:
The passage describes such cases as part of “dirty” input that must be handled during data cleaning [Page 41].

---

questions.question: Which of the following best explains why “ignoring the tuple” is a poor strategy when the missing values are limited to a few attributes rather than many?

options.A: It reduces the dataset size unnecessarily, losing valuable information.
options.B: It violates the assumption of independence among attributes.
options.C: It increases computational complexity of subsequent mining tasks.
options.D: It introduces duplicate records into the dataset.

questions.explanation:
Ignoring tuples discards potentially useful data, especially when only a few attributes are missing, making the method ineffective [Page 6].

---

questions.question: In the context of data cleaning, what is the primary purpose of “smoothing out noise while identifying outliers”?

options.A: To increase the dimensionality of the dataset
options.B: To improve the accuracy of subsequent mining models
options.C: To ensure all attributes have the same scale
options.D: To convert categorical data to numerical form

questions.explanation:
Smoothing noise and detecting outliers are aimed at reducing inaccuracies, thereby improving model performance [Page 6].

---

questions.question: If a data warehouse suffers from “inaccurate, incomplete, and inconsistent data,” which combination of data quality dimensions is being violated, as illustrated in the text?
questions.explanation: The passage explicitly lists accuracy, completeness, and consistency as the three elements defining data quality that are compromised [Page 2].
